newsitem.title: USA: Texas spot power mostly steady, March peak lower.
newsitem.headline: Texas spot power mostly steady, March peak lower.

text.p: Spot bulk power prices in the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) were mostly steady Wednesday although March peak power was said to be lower with a drop in natural gas prices, sources said.
ERCOT firm, peak power for a 16-hour block for Thursday was said to be trading steady at $22.50-23.50 per megawatt hour (MWh), the brokers and marketers said.
Non-firm on peak power for Thursday delivery was notionally pegged steady at $20.00-22.00, the sources said.
Firm off-peak Thursday ERCOT deliveries were pegged steady at $13.00-14.00, while non firm off peak power was assessed unchanged at $11.00-13.00, the sources said.
March ERCOT peak power was talked lower at $20.60-20.90 from $21.00-21.50 on Tuesday, while July/August peak power was talked steady at $24.95-25.25 per MWh, the sources said.
Temperatures in Texas were expected to be seasonable to just below normal for the next two days, then climb to an average of one to five degrees above normal through Sunday.
Also, Houston Lighting and Power's 1,250 megawatt South Texas unit 2 was expected to shut down for planned refueling and maintenance on Feb 7 for a scheduled 35 days.
